name: sol_mccc_8
description: Missing access control validation on cross-chain message receiving functions
question: The source file in `source` defines a function that processes incoming cross-chain messages (e.g., an lzReceive, ccipReceive, or similar callback) but fails to verify that the caller is the trusted messaging endpoint/router and/or fails to validate the origin chain ID and source sender address before executing the message's payload, allowing an attacker to spoof or inject arbitrary cross-chain messages; this excludes functions that already verify the caller is the trusted endpoint/relayer and validate source chain and sender address, and excludes admin-only configuration functions restricted via onlyOwner or similar.
criteria: An lzReceive/_nonblockingLzReceive function executes the decoded payload without checking msg.sender equals the configured LayerZero endpoint address
A ccipReceive function processes the message without validating the sourceChainSelector or sender address against an allow-list
A generic receiveMessage function trusts an arbitrary 'srcAddress' parameter passed in the call instead of checking it against a stored trusted remote address mapping
A cross-chain handler decodes and executes function calls from message data without restricting which contract addresses or selectors are permitted to be invoked
